court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: B.Backiyalakshmi vs The District Registrar on 20 August, 2025

parties.respondent_defendant: The District Registrar, Dindigul, Dindigul District; Sub Registrar, Joint - I Sub-Registrar Office, Dindigul District; S.Krishnamoorthy; Inspector of Police, Woraiyur Police Station, Trichy District; Priya Dharshini (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's driver manipulated her emotionally and psychologically, misrepresenting facts, isolating her from family, and attempting to influence decisions. Petitioner was brainwashed into believing the manipulator had good intentions, which were later discovered to be false.

legal_principles.principle: The ingredients under section 7A of the Hindu Marriage Act must be complied with.
legal_principles.held: Since the marriage has been registered under section 7A of the Hindu Marriage Act, then the ingredients under section 7A ought to have been complied with.

legal_principles.principle: The court must ascertain whether the section 7A has been followed and complied with.
legal_principles.held: The 1st respondent ought to have ascertained whether the section 7A has been followed and complied with, but the document is a printed format wherein the 1st respondent had monotonously registered the same.

outcome.final_order: The impugned marriage registration No. HINDU/DINDIGUL JOINT - I/68/2025 dated 17.02.2025 is quashed as illegal on the grounds of fraud, coercion, misrepresentation, and forgery.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation
quashing a marriage registration due to fraud
seeking nullity of marriage on grounds of coercion
